It seems like a good game, but there is 1 major flaw with it. Once you get to day 14, it locks you out from continuing to play. now, you may say that of course it does, it's a demo. To which i say, the developer chose to publish the demo as a stand alone steam page, and so it should be treated as such. These "demos" are just flooding steam searches when we could instead be finding actually full games listed as free. If you want money for your game, thats fine, no issue there, but having a demo pop up under free is deceptive.

Very fun little dungeon builder game, with charming style and a lot of creativity. It gives you such a good feeling to design a dungeon which you wish for heroes to have a good time completing and finding good loot, fights and exp in the process. There are some minor bugs, which is a freezing at day 10 and some npcs getting stuck in front of useable objects like vendors and chests. I was a bit sad, that after day 14 the game didn't let me play more. Prologues are usually playable infinitelly with the limited stuff they give. This one is sadly not.
14 Playable days is not nearly long enough to unlock all the prologue content that's listed. I would need to see more of the content before I would be interested in the full game.

I love dungeon management type games, and this game scratches that itch real good. There just aren't many games that cover this genre while being fun and relaxing to play. I only wish I could play longer, but I guess I'll have to wait for the game to come out.

"Dungeon Tycoon: Prologue" is not a game. It's an advertisement for a product called "Dungeon Tycoon". Dungeon Tycoon is an as-yet unreleased low poly ripoff of Dungeon Keeper... the tired, old, overdone game where you build the dungeon to stop the heroes coming in and trashing the place, yadda yadda. Except this is considerably worse in all respects than the myriad other Dungeon keeper games. But this isn't completely relevant because this is not Dungeon Tycoon, it's just an advertisment for it, so it's not correct to try to review that completely distinct product. We must instead review this for what it is... an advertisement. If you enjoy advertisements, you can consume them for free on the web or on Youtube without needing to add them to your game library, download them, and then launch the advertising. It's impossible in a general sense to recommend people should do that over playing real, full games on Steam, and that applies here with "Dungeon Tycoon: Prologue" too. The idea here is presumably to gauge whether they should bother making the rest of the game (the studio released another tycoon game that was a massive flop), so there's playing this cautiously. Supporting the fact this is a marketing activity, of course the developer paid for some fake reviews from the review farm in Russia, uncovered by the Sentinels of the Store. Yes, we know when developers pay for reviews. No, it's not legal. This is only free in the same way that adverts on Youtube and banner ads in your browser are. This is a game demo that's been dumped on Steam to advertise another Steam store page in the hopes of raking in some cash. Just because advertisements are free, doesn't mean they're worth your time. It's important to understand there's a formal process to create a demo/page for a game which hasn't been followed here: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/application/demos While it might seem like an inocuous mistake, publishing demos and advertisements as if they are full games is misleading and in some ways harmful. This advertisement is taking up marketing space and visibility that would be better made available to a developer that's done the right thing and created a full game. Instead, that visibility is given over to a demo/advert that's been published incorrectly and is polluting the marketplace. It's unclear if this mistake was made through incompetence or a deliberate intent to mislead gamers. Often developers may choose to incorrectly publish demo/advertisements as separate games as a cheap way to bypass paying Valve for marketing presence on the Steam front page, which may seem clever to them, but it's harmful behaviour and it's not good for gamers. [quote][b][url=https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/federal-register-notices/16-cfr-part-465-trade-regulation-rule-use-consumer-reviews-testimonials-final-rule]Warning: Review Manipulation![/url][/b] This advert features a number of fake positive reviews from accounts known to be in the business of review manipulation/paid reviews. They're all written in either Russian or broken English, appear at almost exactly the same time, very shortly after the game launched on Steam, all have a direct Steam purchase of the game, and the accounts are used consistently to write fake reviews for asset flips and other cash grabs/scams. The "Positive" review score on this game should be disregarded due to this blatant, unethical review manipulation. This is done to deceive and scam gamers into paying for a bad product. Due to the 2024 FTC ruling (16 CFR Part 465), these fake reviews are a violation of US Federal Law.[/quote] Advertisements and incorrectly published demos don't add +1 to your game collector count, they aren't full games. It's impossible for me to recommend this incorrectly published advertising spam to gamers, you deserve better than adverts.
